hypotheses.justification: This can be deleted on its own: only the path component of p in U matters to the based fundamental group. Since hI makes the entire overlap path connected and it contains p, every component of U that meets V is the component of p; any other U-components are disjoint from V and do not affect based loops in X. The descent proof can therefore use paths and frames on the components relevant to p, without requiring all of U to be path connected. The point p still supplies a nonempty relevant component.

Symmetrically, this can be deleted on its own: every component of V meeting U is the component of p, by path connectedness of the overlap, and components disjoint from U do not affect based loops in X. Restricting the descent argument to the components relevant to p gives the same extension and uniqueness. The point p ensures the relevant component is nonempty.
